punchline: Napoleon screamed at him and slammed the door, Talleyrand calmly commented on the Emperor's manners, and then he outlasted him.
thirty_sec: Talleyrand served one French government after another, from the old monarchy through Napoleon and beyond. In 1809 Napoleon found out he'd been discussing the succession and called him a thief, a coward and a traitor in front of witnesses. Talleyrand just remarked that it was a pity such a great man was so badly brought up. He lost a court title, but he later represented France at the Congress of Vienna and was still an ambassador at about eighty, because every regime needed the work he did.
question: If the person who brought you in walked out tomorrow, what would still make you worth keeping?
key_contrast: Loyal to a leader, useful to power
